summary.intent: Execute Phase 65 (SDK Write-Chain, Bin Re-link, and Invite Claim) using wave-based parallel execution across 7 plans in 4 waves, then run the full ship-phase loop (verify, secure, validate, simplify, e2e gate, code review, PR, resolve reviews).
summary.outcome: All 7 plans implemented and verified (4/4 must-haves, 29/29 threats closed, Nyquist compliant), 32 real bugs fixed across 2 rounds of CodeRabbit/greptile review hardening, PR #583 opened with all CI green and 20/20 review threads resolved. A late-breaking greptile finding (Uint8Array serialization bug in bin encrypt/decrypt) was caught and fixed after the PR was open.

repo: Write plane is keyed by node UUID; read plane is keyed by IPNS name — shared-write ops must thread both IDs separately or ops like deleteFromSharedFolder silently no-op on the wrong plane.

`pnpm typecheck` runs the full dependency-ordered build chain (crypto→core→api-client→sdk-core→sdk→web→scripts) and is the correct post-merge build gate; targeted vitest alone misses cross-package type breaks.
SDK E2E test secret is `e2e-test-secret-ci-only` in `apps/api/.env`, not the sdk-e2e default `e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production`; mismatch causes a 401 on test-login.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL); patch PR bodies via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
The husky pre-commit hook is slow enough to trigger a 143 exit (timeout) on `git commit` while the commit still lands; always verify with `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying blindly.
Worktree executor agents don't have all monorepo packages pre-built; their isolated typecheck/test results can miss cross-package breaks that only the full `pnpm typecheck` on the main tree catches.
The `chore(release)` bot commit did not appear on the branch in this run despite Release Preview passing — worth checking before merge in case it self-heals via the preview workflow recompute.
CodeRabbit and greptile are both active reviewers; greptile provides an explicit confidence score and sometimes catches bugs CodeRabbit misses (e.g. the Uint8Array serialization bug).

code.finding: `encryptBinMetadata` was JSON.stringify-ing `nodeReadKey` (a Uint8Array) directly, producing `{"0":..}` object literal instead of the hex string the type doc promised; `decryptBinMetadata` never rebuilt the Uint8Array on read. Fixed by hex-encoding on write (`bytesToHex`) and hex-decoding on read (`hexToBytes`).
Existing encrypt/decrypt round-trip tests used `nodeReadKey: undefined` (pre-Phase-65 baseline), so the serialization bug was invisible until a new `nodeReadKey`-populated round-trip test was added.

`deleteFromSharedFolder` was filtering the write-body's `WriteChildRef` array by `ipnsName` (a k51 string) against `childId` (a UUID) — never matched, leaving a stale `WriteChildRef` that would crash `rotateWriteFromNode` after any shared delete.

Per-node ordering (publish-then-tombstone for the same node) was correct, but child tombstones could fire before the parent was re-pointed. Fixed with a `pendingTombstones: string[]` collector inside `rotateWriteSubtree`; tombstones are fired in `rotateWriteFromNode` only after the full subtree publishes.

`buildSharedWriteContext` still used the old `folderKey`/`ipnsPrivateKey` shape after 65-04 reshaped `SharedWriteContext` to `readKey`/`writeKey`/`publishedNode`/seams — caught only by the post-merge full typecheck, not by the executor's isolated build.

`seedSharedFolder` is reachable from `useSharedNavigation.ts:199` (a live web path); the Phase-68 `PLACEHOLDER_PUBLISHED_NODE` sentinel defaults inserted here are dormant but not dead — Phase-68 must supply real values to prevent silent runtime failures.
`addToBin`'s `nodeRef` object is built from primitives only (strings/numbers), so no Uint8Array fields other than `nodeReadKey` leak into the JSON-serialized bin blob.

workflow: Single-plan waves should run on the main tree to avoid the pnpm install overhead of worktree setup; parallelism only pays when 2+ plans have disjoint file sets.
Post-merge build gate (`pnpm typecheck`) is the critical integration check in a monorepo — it catches cross-plan type breaks that executor-level isolated builds and targeted vitest suites miss.
Background `gh pr checks` polling exits non-zero on transient API blips as well as real failures; always read the output file before treating a poll exit-1 as a failure.
CodeRabbit re-reviews fix commits and can raise new findings in a second wave; budget for a round-2 thread-resolution pass after any substantive fix push.

Mocking `encryptBinMetadata`/`decryptBinMetadata` at the SDK test layer is correct for isolation but makes serialization bugs in the core helpers invisible; real round-trip coverage must live in core-level tests that call the helpers directly.

Parallel worktree fix agents with disjoint file sets merge cleanly, but signature changes (added required params, changed return types) require a full typecheck on the merged tree to surface caller breakage.
Greptile's confidence score is a useful signal: 3/5 on mock-heavy test suites is worth investigating even when all tests pass.

friction: Slow husky pre-commit hook caused `git commit` to exit 143 (timeout) on multiple commits while the commit still landed — silent false-failure that required manual `git log` verification each time.
SDK E2E test-login returned 401 because the default `SDK_E2E_SECRET` env var doesn't match `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` in `apps/api/.env`; wasted a run diagnosing the auth failure.
`SCRATCH` shell variable was not exported to the Node.js child process in bash commands, causing two script failures that required restructuring the commands.
`tail` piped to the typecheck command silently consumed the exit code on the first run, requiring a second run with reliable exit capture.
65-04's `SharedWriteContext` reshape under-scoped its consumers (`context.ts`, `client.ts`, `SharedFolderState`, web bridge), requiring a remediation commit and re-run of the post-merge gate.
Background poll for CI settled with exit code 1 due to a transient `api.github.com` blip, not an actual failure — required re-reading the output file to confirm.
open_items: Phase 68: wire real `publishedNode` and `writeKey` values into `SharedFolderState` and remove `PLACEHOLDER_PUBLISHED_NODE` sentinel; also return updated parent envelope from `resealAndPublishParent` (tracked: `todos/pending/2026-06-30-phase68-shared-write-context-publishednode-wiring.md`, covering PR threads #9/#10/#15/#17).

Phase 66: bin-delete pin-leak (442 MB leaked IPFS pins from `addToBin`/`deleteFromBin` not unpinning content/version CIDs); re-tagged from Phase 65 (`todos/pending/2026-06-23-bin-delete-and-empty-bin-leak-content-and-version-cid-pins.md`).

E2E test seed index-stability: `capturedKeys[0/2]` index-based seed identification in `write-chain-rotation.test.ts` is brittle if ECIES wrapping emits extra 32-byte randoms (`todos/pending/2026-06-30-write-chain-e2e-seed-index-stability.md`).

Pre-existing sdk-e2e type errors in `batch-upload`, `ipns-consistency`, `file-operations` suites from the earlier metadata-refactor (`FolderChild`, `FilePointer`, `SealedChildRef.id/.type` removed); tracked by existing todos.
`client.ts` subtree-IPNS-collect stub (`packages/sdk/src/client.ts:205,216`) logs a non-fatal `not implemented — phase 65 (bin re-link: subtree IPNS collect)` warning; out of Phase 65 scope.
WRITE-04 live publish gate (403/410 rejection on tombstoned IPNS names) is a D-02 mock seam deferred to Phase 66 success criteria.

32-byte input validation on `sealChildWriteKey`/`unsealChildWriteKey` was skipped to avoid diverging from the verbatim 0x02 twin pair that also lacks guards; should be added holistically to all node seal primitives.
Thread #14 (folder-delete subtree write-revocation) requires the unimplemented subtree-IPNS-collect path and is out of Phase 65 scope.
